stories.title: 14 dead in Russian strikes on Kyiv on eve of NATO summit
stories.summary: Russia struck Ukraine's Kyiv region with ballistic missiles in the early hours of this morning, killing at least 14 people and wounding dozens more, authorities said, on the eve of a NATO summit in Turkey. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged his allies to take "strong decisions" at the summit. "It is critically important that the world - first and foremost the United States and our European partners -- come out of the NATO Summit in Ankara with strong decisions in support of our air defence," Mr Zelensky said on Facebook. Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said rescue crews were pulling residents from buildings shattered by the overnight barrage.

stories.title: Motive sought over murder of man in Dún Laoghaire
stories.summary: Gardaí say they are trying to establish a motive for the murder of a 39-year-old man who was shot dead in Dún Laoghaire yesterday. Mark Cullen, who was from Shanganagh Cliffs, Shankill in south Dublin, was shot in the leg at Patrician Park, Kill Avenue in Dún Laoghaire, and died at the scene His is the first gang-related murder this year and the first organised crime gun killing since 2024. Gardaí said they believe that Mr Cullen went to Patrician Park at around 8.30am yesterday morning for a prearranged meeting and was fatally injured during a struggle with a handgun or deliberately shot as part of a dispute or so-called punishment shooting.

stories.title: JD Sports to reissue nearly €250,000 in gift card credit
stories.summary: JD Sports has agreed to reissue nearly €250,000 in unspent gift card credit to Irish consumers, after the company had sold gift cards to them with incorrect expiry dates. This decision follows engagement by the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC) with the UK sportswear retailer on the issue. Under gift voucher legislation introduced in Ireland in December 2019, gift vouchers must be valid for at least five years. However, since the legislation was introduced, gift cards bought online from JD Sports were issued with just a one-year expiry date.

stories.title: Woman in her 50s found dead after assault in Co Laois
stories.summary: A woman aged in her 50s has been found dead following an assault in Co Laois. The incident happened at a house at Church Street, near Main Street, in Portlaoise at around 12.30pm yesterday afternoon. A man in his 70s was arrested at the scene and is being held at Portlaoise Garda Station. The State Pathologist has been notified and a post-mortem examination will be arranged.

stories.title: Maternity advice ensures women's voices are heard - HSE
stories.summary: The Clinical Director of the HSE National Women and Infants Health Programme has said pregnant women's voices are being heard after the former master of the National Maternity Hospital, Dr Peter Boylan, expressed concern that women are being sent home from hospitals while in early labour. "This notion that women may not be listened to or may not be admitted to hospital is absolutely erroneous," Dr Cliona Murphy said. Dr Murphy was responding to comments from Dr Boylan, who said national guidelines around labour must be updated to acknowledge changes to international best practice and evidence. "That's dangerous," said Dr Boylan. He said it is no longer international best practice to adopt this approach.

stories.title: Fans banned from Tour de France stage amid wildfires
stories.summary: Wildfires are continuing to rage across southern Europe, forcing thousands of people to evacuate their homes and prompting officials to ban spectators from a stage of the Tour de France. Hundreds of firefighters are battling blazes that have devastated more than 19,000 hectares of land - an area more than twice the size of Manhattan - across Portugal, Spain, France and Greece. Temperatures are on the rise again, predicted to reach 40C in parts of a region still suffering the aftermath of a recent record-breaking heatwave. In southwestern France near the city of Perpignan, 700 firefighters backed by special aircraft battled to control a "gigantic" blaze spreading in a hard-to-reach remote area, with more than 10,000 local residents evacuated.
